title: Open Problem (edge-EP property characterization for planar graph expansions)
statement_text: Finding a characterization for the planar graphs $J$ such that $J$-expansions have the edge-Erd\H{o}s-P\'osa property remains an intriguing open problem.
context_text: A class $\mathcal{H}$ of graphs has the vertex-Erdős–Pósa property (resp. edge-Erdős–Pósa property, edge-EP property) if there is a bounding function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}$ such that for every $k$, every graph $G$ contains either $k$ vertex-disjoint (resp. edge-disjoint) subgraphs belonging to $\mathcal{H}$, or a set $F$ of at most $f(k)$ vertices (resp. edges) such that $G-F$ has no subgraph in $\mathcal{H}$. For a graph $J$, a $J$-expansion is a graph that contains $J$ as a minor. Robertson and Seymour showed that $J$-expansions have the vertex-EP property if and only if $J$ is planar (and an $O(k\log k)$ bounding function is now known). Planarity of $J$ is also necessary for the edge version. The edge-EP property is known for $\theta_r$-expansions ($\theta_r$ being two vertices joined by $r$ parallel edges), for $K_4$-expansions and for long cycles (cycles of length at least $\ell$), for which the authors give a bounding function $O(k\ell\log(k\ell))$ via a ball-packing technique. On the other hand, Bruhn, Heinlein and Joos showed that $J$-expansions do not have the edge-EP property when $J$ is a ladder with at least $71$ rungs or a subcubic tree of pathwidth at least $19$. The question was raised by Raymond, Sau and Thilikos and by Bruhn, Heinlein and Joos.
notes: Stated in prose in the introduction as 'an intriguing open problem'; no labelled theorem environment. Section 5, which the paper explicitly announces contains further open problems, appears to be missing from the PDF extraction — additional items likely exist there.
